title: Generated agreement versions: does the change between version A and version B alter the answer for the case?
decision: for a case with a yes/no point at issue, whether the answer is the same under both versions of an agreement, yes only under version A, or yes only under version B
licence: generated by the benchmark's script (no third-party text)
skill: compare two versions of an agreement clause by clause (numbers may shift) and decide from the exact limit wording whether the change alters the yes/no answer for a concrete case
knobs: clauses per version 8 / 10-11 / 12-14; moved clause (levels 2-3) and inserted clause (level 3) shift the numbering; a third changed clause and decoy facts; two-condition requests (level 3); limit wordings that count or do not count the stated figure; facts on or one step from a stated figure
notes: Metric pair_accuracy: a group counts as solved only when every case of it is answered correctly (chance = the mean over groups of (1/3)^members). Reason: the direction of the change of the topic clause and the polarity of the point at issue decide every case whose fact lies between the two limits (two thirds of the items), so a reader who never looks at the facts of the case reaches 0.667 item accuracy, but such a reader solves no group that contains a same case (1 of 201 groups). Item accuracy is still reported by score.py's calibration columns. 600 items in 201 groups: per level 66 groups of three cases (one per class) on one version pair and one group of two (200 items is not a multiple of 3; level 1 leaves out yes_only_B, level 2 same, level 3 yes_only_A), so every class has 200 items and every level 200 (classes 67/66/67 per level). Members of a group share the two versions and differ in the case paragraph only (same lines; values of the facts and the point at issue). Every convention is written in the state. Answer computed from the structured specification (meta.spec). State length 2778 to 5050 characters (median 3730).
